nodes.name: Room Temperature Vulcanization Corrosion
nodes.procedure: Initially, a rough Ni3S2 transition layer was in situ grown on the surface of NM by room temperature vulcanization. The NM was immersed in a sodium thiosulfate buffer (pH = 4) for 10 hours.

nodes.description: Standard OER characterization in 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The resultant NiFe-LDH/Ni3S2 heterostructure manifests remarkable OER performance, with ultra-low overpotentials of 202 mV at 10 mAcm-2 and 290 mV at 800 mAcm-2 in 1.0 M KOH at 25 °C

electrocatalytic performance was further evaluated under industrially relevant conditions, e.g., 80 °C in 30 wt% KOH solution... the NiFe-LDH/Ni3S2 heterostructure electrode displays superior activity, requiring an overpotential of merely 235 mV to achieve 800 mA cm-2
The NiFe-LDH/Ni3S2 PPS Raney Ni electrolyzer achieves a large current density of 800 mA cm-2 at a cell voltage of 1.908 V... sustains its performance after 40 h of continuous operation at 800 mA cm-2

nodes.characterization_summary: UPS determined work functions of 3.01 eV for Ni3S2 and 2.48 eV for NiFe-LDH, creating a work function difference of 0.53 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: UPS was utilized to obtain work functions (Φ) values of Ni3S2 and NiFe-LDH ... The calculated Φ values are 3.01 eV for Ni3S2 and 2.48 eV for NiFe-LDH, indicating a substantial ΔΦ of 0.53 eV

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows upward binding energy shifts of 0.5 eV (Ni 2p) and 0.4 eV (Fe 2p) in the heterostructure, confirming electron transfer from NiFe-LDH to Ni3S2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: NiFe-LDH/Ni3S2 shows upward shifts of 0.5 and 0.4 eV of the binding energy in the Ni 2p and Fe 2p region compared with those of NiFe-LDH

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS Nyquist plots show NiFe-LDH/Ni3S2 has the smallest charge-transfer resistance (Rct) and reduced ohmic resistance (Rohm).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The NiFe-LDH/Ni3S2 heterostructure displays the smallest charge-transfer resistance (Rct) in the EIS Nyquist plots ... yield a marked reduction in ohmic resistance (Rohm) compared to NiFe-LDH

nodes.characterization_summary: The electrochemical double-layer capacitance (Cdl) was 1.96 mF/cm2, used to estimate the ECSA and active site density.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cdl value of NiFe-LDH/Ni3S2 is calculated to be 1.96 mF cm−2, noticeably larger than those of NiFe-LDH, Ni3S2, and NM.

properties.description: Linear fitting of capacitive current density against scan rate to estimate electrochemical active surface area (ECSA).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows accelerated phase transition to γ-NiOOH for the heterostructure and confirms Fe-O signal retention vs leaching in pure NiFe-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The NiFe-LDH/Ni3S2 demonstrates pronounced spectral changes at lower potentials ... the former retains a discernible Fe-O peak and NO3− signal (Figure 4d).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS measurements show that the heterostructure mitigates Fe leaching compared to the rapid leaching observed in pure NiFe-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ICP-MS monitored the amount of Fe dissolution ... NiFe-LDH exhibits rapid Fe leaching, and by the introduction of BEF, a slow Fe leaching is displayed in NiFe-LDH/Ni3S2

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping shows the uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, and S across the heterostructure interface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM image and EDS mapping of NiFe-LDH/Ni3S2 ... confirm the uniform distribution of NiFe-LDH on the Ni3S2 layer
